# DocuExtract

> PDF Invoice to Excel Extractor. Converts invoice PDFs into structured XLSX, CSV and JSON entirely in the browser.

## Product facts

DocuExtract is a browser-based invoice PDF extractor. Application code processes files locally and does not upload them to an application backend. The application has no account, backend, database, analytics or telemetry.

Available exports:
- XLSX: full invoice.
- JSON: full invoice.
- CSV: line items only.

Current features include a review screen before export, date-confirmation flags, Zod-validated data and formula-injection sanitization on exports.

## Support matrix

- Text-based PDFs: supported.
- Multi-page text-based PDFs: supported up to 100 pages.
- Scanned and image-only PDFs: not currently supported; OCR is planned for Phase 2.
- Password-protected PDFs: encrypted files are rejected unless already decrypted.
- Corrupt PDFs: not supported.
- Handwritten invoices: recognition is not guaranteed.
- Multiple invoices in one PDF: not supported; planned for Phase 2.

## Important limitations

Extraction is heuristic. Every output must be reviewed before accounting, tax, payment or legal use.

Labels and values must be on the same line or in neighbouring columns of the same row. Layouts with a label above its value are not read.

Numeric dates such as 05/09/2026 are interpreted as DD/MM/YYYY and flagged for confirmation.

Line items are detected from column gaps and the table header. Unusual tables may need manual correction on the review screen.

The current workflow supports one invoice per PDF. CSV exports line items only; XLSX and JSON contain the full invoice.

## Privacy

Invoice data is not written to URLs, localStorage or sessionStorage. PDF buffers are released and documents are destroyed after processing. React rendering does not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Users can inspect browser network activity to verify observed application requests.

## Licensing and status

DocuExtract v1.0.0 is open source under the MIT License. The developer plans to offer future production versions under a commercial licence. Versions already released under MIT remain available under MIT.
